data.title: The Present Perfect Tense
data.rule: Use the present perfect for an action completed in the recent past whose result matters now.

examples.note: have — with I / you / we / they

narration: Now let us learn a tense we use every single day. {{b1}} We use the present perfect tense when an action is complete, but its result still matters now. If I say my homework is done, the doing is over, but the result is with me right now. {{b2}} Here is the pattern to remember: the subject, then has or have, then the third form of the verb, the past participle. {{b3.1}} Look at the first example. She has finished her homework. She is singular, so we use has, and finished is the third form. {{b3.2}} And the second: They have gone to the market. They is plural, so we use have, and gone is the third form of go. Remember: has for he, she and it, and have for everyone else.
